doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Other Piano Jazz guests: Red Richards, Harold Mabern and Cliff Smalls
summary: She recalls Ralph Sharon and Red Richards, a steady jazz historian who worked with Jimmy, and mentions Harold Mabern and Cliff Smalls as people she wants for the show.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And did you ever have someone like Ralph Sharon or Red Richards or someone?

I had Ralph Sharon. Red Richards. I feel so bad about him, because he worked with Jimmy all the time. I knew him very well. He did a wonderful “Piano Jazz” show, because it’s so historical. Do you have that one?
I think I do have that one.

There’s a piece of jazz history. That guy. Worked all his life. Never was known to the public. But very solid citizen. Stayed . . . still married to the same woman. People always thing of musicians as being such rapscallions.
It sounds like Harold Mabern or someone who’s very steady, very consistent. Class act all the time.
Yeah. Absolutely. There’s another guy I didn’t think of. Harold Mabern. There’s a guy. He’s doing an awful lot. Cliff Smalls. Do you know him?

He . . . I’m trying to think, who he worked with. He’s somebody that . . . Stanley Dance is always saying to me, “Why don’t you have Cliff Smalls,” and I’ve tried, but he’s always working somewhere, gone to Japan or something
